searchText: should we spec this out? like a special section kind is reserved for declaring capabilities Here's a spec we can riff on - https://hackmd.io/@shemnon/RIP-EOF-Capabilities/edit I feel like the signalling should at least be more dense and not involve string parsing Like we can't expect to be able to write completely initcode binary portable contracts, having the target evm do checks to ensure it's safe to run but we can probably figure out some reasonable sanity checking (a) How do we make space for arbitrary spec names? OPIPS, AIPs, ZKIPs, etc. (b) how do we accommodate versioning systems without forcing 8-bit 3 part semver? Human readable solves these issues. Not all changes will be RIPs/EIPs, some will have chain-specific changes. That alone starts the human readable path. Parameters can be dense. what's wrong with forcing 3 byte semver? even that's probably too sophisticated (a) calver is a thing, (b) not all xIPs may have 7577 versioning Note the git hash accomodation all we really care about is being able to sanity check that specific features are available and match what's expected And make it extensible without centralized registration. I haven't read the full eip yet fwiw This is good fodder for the rationale section, which I haven't written yet. I also expect most clients to do simple binary matching. i.e. these binary capabilities are supported and do a prefix match. So wheter it's dense or human readable in code it's all prefix match to the params or full content match if no params. I don't think we will see EVMs supporting multiple versions of the same capability reaching production status.
